pathways.name: TNF-alpha Signaling
pathways.description: The dominant inflammatory pathway in RA. TNF-alpha produced by synovial macrophages and fibroblasts binds TNFR1/TNFR2, activating NF-κB and MAP kinase cascades. This drives production of IL-6, IL-1, MMPs, and RANKL, creating a self-amplifying inflammatory loop in the synovium.

pathways.name: IL-6 / JAK-STAT Signaling
pathways.description: IL-6 is the second dominant cytokine in RA, driving systemic inflammation (CRP, hepcidin, thrombocytosis), synovial pannus formation, and Th17 polarization. IL-6 signals through gp130-IL-6R complexes activating JAK1/JAK2/TYK2 -> STAT3. JAK inhibitors block multiple cytokine signals simultaneously.

pathways.name: T Cell Costimulation & Activation
pathways.description: CD4+ T cells are abundant in RA synovium and provide help to B cells and macrophages. CD28 costimulation (B7.1/B7.2 binding) is required for full T cell activation. CTLA4 competitively inhibits this interaction. Abatacept (CTLA4-Ig) blocks T cell costimulation. T cell-derived RANKL drives osteoclastogenesis.

pathways.name: B Cell Signaling & Autoantibody Production
pathways.description: B cells in RA synovium form ectopic germinal centers producing anti-CCP and RF autoantibodies. BAFF promotes B cell survival. CD20+ B cells present antigen to T cells. Rituximab depletes CD20+ B cells. BLK and BANK1 regulate BCR signaling thresholds.

pathways.name: Complement System & Immune Complex Deposition
pathways.description: Immune complexes (RF-IgG and anti-CCP-citrullinated antigen) activate classical complement in RA synovium. C5a is a potent chemoattractant recruiting neutrophils to the joint. TRAF1/C5 locus links complement to RA genetic risk.

pathways.name: NF-κB Inflammatory Pathway
pathways.description: NF-κB is the central transcriptional hub integrating TNF, IL-1, TLR, and RANKL signals in RA. REL and RELA subunits drive expression of TNF, IL-6, IL-1β, MMPs, and COX-2. TNFAIP3 (A20) normally limits NF-κB activation; A20 variants impair this negative regulation.

pathways.name: Citrullination & Autoantigen Generation
pathways.description: PADI4 (peptidyl arginine deiminase 4) catalyzes conversion of arginine to citrulline in proteins. In RA, PADI4 is activated in the inflamed synovium, generating citrullinated autoantigens (vimentin, fibrinogen, α-enolase). HLA-DRB1 shared epitope alleles preferentially present citrullinated peptides to T cells, breaking tolerance and driving anti-CCP antibody production.

pathways.name: Bone Erosion & Osteoclast Activation
pathways.description: Bone erosion is the hallmark of destructive RA. Synovial fibroblasts and activated T cells express RANKL, which binds RANK on osteoclast precursors, driving their differentiation into mature bone-resorbing osteoclasts. TNF, IL-6, and IL-1 synergistically enhance RANKL-mediated osteoclastogenesis.
